body.summary: An episodic supernatural series following Ginko, a wandering mushishi who travels a rural, pre-modern Japan-like countryside diagnosing and settling troubles caused by mushi, primordial life-forms between matter and spirit that ordinary people cannot see. Each episode is largely self-contained: a villager, child or craftsman is afflicted, and the resolution often asks the human to change their life rather than destroy the creature. Ginko's own origin is revealed in fragments, and the series ends on his continued wandering. ||His childhood is shown to begin when he was swallowed by a Tokoyami and lost his memories; he took the name of the light-mushi that gave him his one pale eye.||

arcs.summary: Ginko's fragmentary origin: swallowed by a Tokoyami, losing his memory, taking the name of the light-mushi and one pale eye.
The Karibusa scribe Tanyuu and the forbidden mushi sealed in her body, tended by the Minai clan.
Kumado's soul is replaced by an artificial mushi and he is nearly consumed by Sanekui in a Path of Overgrowth.
Kaya is chosen as mountain lord, returns the power to the mountain and ceases to be herself.

the cost of a place's prosperity
humans as one part of nature

notable_scenes.summary: Ginko explains mushi with his hand, thumb to wrist, placing man at the fingertip.
Shinra draws the green wine cup with his left hand and his grandmother becomes whole.
Sui opens her eyes with her second eyelids closed and the moonlight lures the mushi out.
Maho holds his ears and hears the rumble of his own muscles, his mother's sound.
Jin cuts his pillow and the dream-world nest spills out.
The travelling swamp is netted at the river mouth and Io is pulled out as a pearl-like form.
Kourou touches the Kouda and is engulfed by the rising stream.
Ginko tells of the Tokoyami and the moon that set and rose again, and how he took his name.
Kaya's brother hears the bells and the mountain lord returns to the law.
